meta.title: recap-retrieve · type-safe AI
meta.lede: The last teaching beat of a film: one retrieval question about content from earlier, a pause, the answer read off the film’s own object, a recap in pictures, and a return to the opening case.
meta.synthesis: The answer is never typed in: it is counted off the persistent object (2,000 × 0.99¹⁰, junction by junction). The recap is three small drawings of earlier frames, not a list. The return re-runs the opening instance, Marisol’s invoice, with the new model applied.
sources: archive/films/typesafe — the opening case and the compounding chapter

head.title: One question, then the way back

params.question: At 0.99 per step, how many of 2,000 runs arrive after 10 steps?

recap.line: the mask closes the off-schema tracks
a type checks the shape, not the facts

foot.ask: retrieval first: answer before the film does
foot.recap: three frames from earlier, as pictures
foot.return: Marisol’s invoice again: constrained, every field well-typed

captions.ask: One question about the compounding chapter. Pause and answer it.
captions.answer: Count it off the chain: 2,000 at 0.99 per step leaves 1,809.
captions.hold: About 90 %: a better rate per step, still compounding.
captions.recap: Three things to keep: the mask, the staircase, the shape check.
captions.return: And the opening invoice, now constrained: every field well-typed.

meta.title: recap-retrieve · anchoring
meta.lede: A retrieval question about Kahneman’s wheel of fortune: rigged to stop at 10 or 65, it moved people’s estimates of a fact. The answer is read off the piles; the return puts both piles back side by side.
meta.synthesis: Asked after a delay, the question forces recall instead of recognition. The answer comes from the persistent object (the pile under the 10), the recap is three small drawings, and the return shows both piles again: same question, same facts, a 20-point difference.
sources: Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow, ch. 11 (Anchors)

x.label: % OF UN MEMBERS THAT ARE AFRICAN

params.question: The wheel stopped at 10. Which mean did that group give: 25 % or 45 %?

recap.line: a number with no meaning came first
we adjust away from it, and stop too soon

returnLines: Wheel at 10, a mean of 25 %. Wheel at 65, a mean of 45 %.
Same question, same facts: only the anchor changed.

foot.ask: pause and answer · the wheel was a while ago
foot.answer: the group that saw 10 guessed {answer} on average
foot.recap: three frames from earlier, as pictures
foot.return: the anchor moved the average by 20 points

notes: the dots are an illustrative spread around the published means (Kahneman ch. 11)

captions.ask: Before the recap, one question. Pause and answer it.
captions.answer: Read it off the piles: the group that saw 10 said 25 % on average.
captions.hold: A meaningless number, and the estimates followed it.
captions.recap: Three things to keep: the wheel, the piles, the short adjustment.
captions.return: Both groups again: same question, same facts, 20 points apart.
